stories.headline: UK and EU agree three deals at a Brussels summit
GTA 6 sells an estimated $2.36 billion at launch

beats.narr: Prime Minister Andy Burnham met EU leaders in Brussels.
They agreed three deals, one for young people.
Then lunch: battered North Sea cod and chips.
Then a Brussels waffle, with fruit.

n261120a.end: Rick held out against Europe until pudding.
n261120a.title: Rick declares war on a waffle. Loses.
n261120a.claim: Prime Minister Andy Burnham and EU leaders agreed three deals at a summit in Brussels on Friday, on food and drink trade, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme: the biggest step towards the EU since Brexit.
n261120a.why: Britain left the EU in 2020, after a 2016 vote. The EU says the three deals will not come into force until the UK gives EU students the fees British students pay.
facts: Three deals: food and drink, emissions, youth
Up to 100,000 under-30s each way, for 3 years
Burnham: +0.5% to GDP, a £17bn boost
EU: none in force without equal tuition fees
Six months set aside to settle the fees
Lunch: cod and chips, then a Brussels waffle

Analysts estimate 24.5 million copies, worth about $2.36 billion.
UK PS5 downloads peaked at 8.6 times normal.
The game is 212 gigabytes.

n261120e.why: Rockstar and its parent, Take-Two, have not released sales figures; Sensor Tower's estimate rests on email receipts. GTA 5 made $1 billion in its first three days in 2013.

beats.narr: The Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday.
In March they signed him: two years, $88 million.
They kept him at the trade deadline. Two games later, released.
$50 million of it was guaranteed.

n261120g.end: Rick has asked to be released. He was never signed.
n261120g.title: Rick's take: worst move ever, then best
n261120g.claim: The Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday, a day after he was benched in a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans; Anthony Richardson Sr. will start next.
n261120g.why: Jones signed a two-year, $88 million contract in March, $50 million of it guaranteed. The Colts kept him at this month's trade deadline, then released him two games later.
facts: Thursday's score: Texans 26, Colts 3
Contract: two years, $88 million, signed March
$50 million of it guaranteed at signing
Colts are 3-8: six losses in seven games
Kept at the deadline; released two games later
Next start: Anthony Richardson Sr., Nov. 29

beats.narr: Britain quietly protected tens of thousands of fridges from hackers.
The fridges' controllers had a weak password problem.
Some staff pulled out the cables and checked temperatures by hand.

n261120h.end: Every fridge was thanked. Tabby's password is still Tabby.
n261120h.title: Posy reassures a fridge in aisle six
n261120h.claim: A secret UK operation has secured tens of thousands of fridges and freezers at supermarkets, restaurants and stadiums from hackers, after researchers found a flaw in their controllers in late October, the BBC reported.
n261120h.why: Three waves of hacks on fridge controllers this year spoiled tonnes of food in Europe. Some UK sites closed the gap by pulling out internet cables and checking temperatures by hand.
facts: Tens of thousands of fridges and freezers secured
France's supermarkets were hit on 11 and 12 October
Three waves of fridge hacks so far in 2026
The controllers had a weak password problem
One chain took hundreds of devices offline a day
Ken Munro: crooks were likely "a matter of days" off

beats.narr: A newspaper taste-tested supermarket fish fingers.
Each brand was baked 12 to 14 minutes at 200C.
M&S got full marks, at £2.50. Bird's Eye was 40p cheaper.

n261120i.end: The fish fingers were tabled. They are now cold.
n261120i.title: Point of order: the fish finger
n261120i.claim: A Mirror taste test of supermarket fish fingers gave full marks to M&S's, at £2.50, ranking them just ahead of Bird's Eye, which came in 40p cheaper.
n261120i.why: Every brand was baked for 12 to 14 minutes at 200C so the test was fair. The tester found Sainsbury's about half the thickness of rivals such as M&S.
facts: Every brand: 12 to 14 minutes at 200C
Winner: M&S, given full marks
The winners cost £2.50
Bird's Eye: "incredibly close", 40p cheaper
Sainsbury's: about half the thickness
